name: Southwest Face
approach: From Trinity Trailhead (2,800 ft) at the end of Chiwawa River Road/FR 6200, follow the Buck Creek Trail (#1513) roughly 9-9.5 miles, climbing through forest, an old avalanche debris field (~4,500 ft), and past an unmarked junction with the Pass No Pass way-trail (bears right, ~5,800 ft). Continue up the way-trail to Pass No Pass (~6,400 ft) and the alpine camping benches beyond, from which Fortress's southwest face and south ridge come into view. Note: since 2026, storm damage has closed FR 6200 to vehicles beyond Atkinson Flat Campground (about mile 16), adding roughly 7 miles of road-walking each way before even reaching the trailhead.

approach_variants.name: Buck Creek Trail #1513 and the Pass No Pass way-trail
approach_variants.notes:
From Trinity Trailhead at 2,800 ft, follow Buck Creek Trail #1513 roughly nine to nine and a half miles, climbing through forest and an old avalanche debris field near 4,500 ft.

The turn is the thing to watch for and it is not marked: an unmarked junction with the Pass No Pass way-trail bears right at about 5,800 ft. Follow the way-trail to Pass No Pass near 6,400 ft and the alpine camping benches beyond it, from which the face and the south ridge come into view.

Since 2026 storm damage has closed FR-6200 to vehicles beyond Atkinson Flat Campground around mile 16, adding roughly seven miles of road-walking each way before you even reach the trailhead.

From a high camp in the Pass No Pass basin, parties report about three and a half to four hours up and two and a half to three back.
approach_variants.season: Jun-Oct, best Jul-Sep once the south-west face has melted out; an axe and sometimes crampons for early-season snow on the approach slopes below the pass
hazards: The direct south-west gully is the loosest ground on the mountain and is directly above anyone below
Steep snow on the approach slopes below Pass No Pass into early summer, needing self-arrest skills
An unmarked way-trail junction at about 5,800 ft that is easy to walk past on a nine-mile approach
Creek crossings and brushy, indistinct trail lower down
Roughly seven extra miles of road-walking each way while FR-6200 is closed beyond Atkinson Flat
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The pass is where the mountain becomes visible, and that is the arrival test: from Pass No Pass and the benches beyond it, Fortress's south-west face and south ridge come into view. Below the pass you cannot see the peak at all. If you are still walking with no mountain in front of you, you have not crossed it.

The climbing starts at a change of surface, not at a feature. From the basin below the pass, green slopes and scree steepen into Class 2-3 talus and slab. There is no step, no toe and no notch to arrive at — grass gives way to rock and that is the base.

The negative marker is the most useful sentence on this route: the direct gully up the face is the loosest ground on the mountain. If you are in a defined gully with rubble moving under every step, you are on the line to avoid, not the line to take. Angle right onto slabbier rock, or follow the south ridge crest instead. A party in 2015 found and cairned an alternate Class 3 line over more solid blocky terrain to skier's right of the gully, and later parties have followed it — so cairns on solid blocky ground here are a good sign, which is the reverse of the situation in the gully.

The discriminator against the other side of this peak: the East Ridge is reached from the Chiwawa-Fortress col at about 7,200 ft, approached cross-country off the Chiwawa River Trail, and it starts with a loose Class 3-4 gully onto a crest of notably better rock. Nothing on that route involves a way-trail or a named pass. If you walked over a pass to get here, you are on the south-west side.

The summit block is talus. There is no technical finish on this route; if you are looking at a fourth-class step you have wandered onto the east side's ground.
